AgentCardView.description:
The definition on the decision that adds a suggested agent (spec 3.3 §5.7 "The decision
that adds an agent", S-I13): every field, from the inbox entry the kernel wrote, never from
the model.

abilities.description: What it can do, in plain words.

allowedWithoutAsking.description: What it would start with: "Nothing yet".

compared.description: "It can do no more than ADK-Rust, and has no shell or web."

id.description: The id the suggested agent would get: what **Change it first** replaces. Never shown.

instructions.description: The instructions, quoted, cut short past the call limit.

instructionsTruncated.description: The instructions are cut short: they must be expanded before the agent can be added.

lines.description:
The definition, one line per field: area, how much it asks first, what it runs on,
files, shell, web, packs, drivers, the daily limit.

AgentChoices.description:
What a person may choose for an agent on this kernel (spec 3.3 §5.7, decision 21): the
models of the providers whose key the kernel has, the packs, the areas and the colours.

models.description: The models, the primary agent's first.

AgentColor.description: An agent's colour: one of the eight avatar colours, never a free value (spec 3.3 §5.7).

AgentConfirmOptionsRequest.description:
`POST /surface/agents/confirm/options` body: the change the person is about to confirm —
`addAgent` or `changeAgent` with the digest its preview showed — bound on the server to
exactly this command (spec 3.3 §7.2: the web home adds an agent at high risk after
confirming it is you).

AgentDetail.description: One agent a person added (spec 3.3 §5.7): what **Settings** shows.

agent.description: The agent as threads and decisions name it.

cantStart.description: Why the kernel cannot build it: "No key for Anthropic".

changedOn.description:
The surface it was last changed on — `web`, `terminal`, `phone` — when the kernel
knows it; a change refused as out of date names it.

granted.description:
What the home lets it do beyond its definition, "On this home it can also:", from the
uses the host granted every agent it runs; empty for an agent that does not run, and
absent when empty (spec 3.3 §5.7, S-I12, S-I13).

id.description: Its kernel target, for commands. Never shown.

mode.description: How much it asks first, with its words.

originText.description: "Added by you on 25 Oct", or "Suggested by ADK-Rust, added by you on 25 Oct".

state.description: Where it is in its life.

version.description: The version a change is made against. Never shown.

AgentDraft.description:
An agent's definition as **Set it up yourself** and **Settings** edit it, in the order of
spec 3.3 §5.7 "The definition".

description.description: What it does, in one line.

model.description: What it runs on; none for the primary agent's model.

AgentLife.description: Where an agent is in its life, as a surface shows it (spec 3.3 §5.7, §8.1).

oneOf.description: Suggested by an agent and waiting for a person.

AgentPreview.description:
**Here is what Finance can do** (spec 3.3 §5.7): what a change lets an agent do, its risk,
and the digest the change is confirmed with.

abilities.description: What it can do, one plain sentence each.

code.description: The first six characters of the digest: the terminal's `--confirm` code.

digest.description: The digest the change applies with. Never shown.

id.description: The agent's kernel target; for an agent not added yet, the id it would get. Never shown.

needsPresence.description: Confirming needs presence: "Confirm it's you" in the home, or a paired local terminal.

widens.description:
The change lets the agent do more: it needs what adding it at that risk needs, and it
first ends the agent's waiting decisions.

oneOf.description: Adding an agent: **Set it up yourself**, or **Change it first** on a suggestion.

replaces.description: The suggestion it replaces, when it came from **Change it first**.

oneOf.description: Changing an agent at the version seen.
Removing an agent at the version seen.

AgentRef.description: An agent as a decision or a thread names it.

displayName.description: The name to show, such as "Finance".

name.description: The agent's name in the runtime.

added.description:
An agent the person added: it has settings beyond its mode and rules (spec 3.3 §5.7).
Absent when false.

area.description: Its area, for an agent the person added (spec 3.3 §5.7).

canChange.description: The caller may change it here (spec 3.3 §7.2). Absent when false.

mode.description: How much it asks first, for an agent the person added (spec 3.3 §5.7).

sessionId.description: The session of its latest work, to open its thread.

statusText.description: The status word: "Working", "Waiting for you", "Asleep until 07:00", "Done", "Failed".

wakeAt.description: When it wakes, while asleep with a wake time.

oneOf.description: "Waiting for you": waiting with a held call.
"Asleep until 07:00": waiting with a wake set, or parked by a stop.
"Ready": an agent the person added that has not run yet (spec 3.3 §5.7, §8.1).
"Can't start": an agent the kernel cannot build (spec 3.3 §5.7, §8.1).

canAdd.description:
The roster ends with **New agent**: the source keeps agents a person adds and the
caller may add one here (spec 3.3 §5.7). Absent when false.

primary.description:
The agent a message goes to when the person names none: the tray's "Ask Finance"
(spec 3.3 §5.5). Absent when the source has no single primary agent.

removed.description:
The agents the person removed, whose threads stay readable through "Removed agents"
at the roster's foot (spec 3.3 §5.7). Absent when none.

Allowed.description: The answers a surface may give one decision (spec 3.3 §7.2).

cancelWindowSecs.description: A spoken "allow once" takes effect after this many seconds unless cancelled.

note.description: Why this surface cannot approve, in plain words, when it cannot.

openInHome.description: Some answers are only in the home: show "Open in home".

options.description: The answers, in the order of §7.1: allow once, always allow, edit, deny.

oneOf.description: Run it and allow the same call from now on, scoped.

AnswerOption.description: One answer a surface may offer, with its label (spec 3.3 §8.2).

needsExpanded.description: The call must be expanded first: it is shown truncated.

needsPresence.description: The person must confirm it is them first (high risk on the web home and the phone).

AnswerRequest.description:
`POST /surface/decisions/{id}/answer` body: an answer from a paired device, at the version
it saw (spec 3.3 §7.2, S-I2).

expanded.description: The device showed the call in full (§7.1).

reason.description: Why, for a `deny`; reported to the agent.

AppAnswer.description:
The home's answer to an `AppRequest`: the JSON-RPC `result` or `error` the page passes
back to the app, and what it shows the person.

error.description: The JSON-RPC error, when it did not.

prompt.description: What the page shows the person.

result.description: The JSON-RPC result, when the request succeeded.

oneOf.description: Its HTML shows a decision's words: "This app was blocked: it shows approval buttons".

It loads or connects to a site its declaration does not list, or declares one in a form
this home does not accept.
It asks to reach this computer, its network, or the home itself.
Its resource is not an MCP App's HTML.

AppError.description: A JSON-RPC error for an app.

AppMessageRequest.description:
`POST /surface/genui/sessions/{session}/apps/{call}/message`: the person pressed **Send
it** on what an app suggested (spec 3.3 §6.1 `genui-apps`). The home sends it as the
person's message, inside an untrusted-content block labelled as the app's suggestion.

AppOpen.description:
What `GET /surface/genui/sessions/{session}/apps/{call}` answers (spec 3.3 §6.1
`genui-apps`): the app to frame, why it was blocked, or that it is not shown here.

oneOf.description: Frame `frameUrl`, on the apps origin, sandboxed.

frameOrigin.description: The apps origin, which the page frames and nothing else.

frameUrl.description: The app's page on the apps origin.

maxHeight.description: The tallest the frame grows, in CSS pixels.

prefersBorder.description: Whether the app asked for a border around it.

refusedPermissions.description: The device permissions it asked for, all refused here.

toolInput.description: The arguments of the call that showed it: `ui/notifications/tool-input`.

oneOf.description: Not shown: "This app was blocked: it shows approval buttons".

detail.description: The technical reason, for the developer panel.

oneOf.description:
Not shown on this surface or without an apps origin: "Open the home on this computer
to see this app", and the tool's text result.

AppPrompt.description:
What the page shows a person for an app's request (spec 3.3 §6.1 `genui-apps`): the app
only ever asks; the person's own press does what it asks.

oneOf.description: A plain notice under the app: "The app tried to use transfer_funds. Apps can't use it."
"The app wants to send: “…”", with **Send it** and **Not now**.

note.description: "It will be marked as suggested by the app".

text.description: "The app wants to send: “Remind me to take an umbrella tomorrow.”"

AppRequest.description:
A request an app made of the home, as the page relays it: `POST
/surface/genui/sessions/{session}/apps/{call}/requests` (spec 3.3 §6.1 `genui-apps`). Only
requests with an `id` reach the home; the page answers notifications itself.

AppView.description:
An app an MCP server's tool showed in a thread (spec 3.3 §6.1 `genui-apps`): on the normal
card background, labelled as unable to approve anything. The page opens it sandboxed on a
second origin; the phone, the terminal and chat show its text result instead.

agent.description: The agent whose call showed it.

appName.description: The server as a person reads it: "Weather".

callId.description: The call that showed it: the app's id in its session.

elsewhereText.description: "Open the home on this computer to see this app": where the app is not shown.

headerText.description: "App from Weather · it can't approve anything".

resultText.description: The tool's text result, which every surface can show.

server.description: The MCP server, by its name on this home.

terminalText.description: "app from Weather · open it in the home": the terminal's line.

tool.description: The tool that showed it, by its name on the server.

AreaChoice.description: An area a person may put an agent in.

mode.description: Its mode: an agent there asks at least this much.

Avatar.description: An agent's avatar: a rounded monogram in the agent's own colour (spec 3.3 §9).

lines.description: One line per event, oldest first.

recorded.description:
The source keeps an activity record. Without one, `lines` is empty whatever ran, so a
surface says nothing is recorded rather than that nothing happened.

BriefingLine.description: One line of "While you were away", from one `/proc` ledger row (spec 3.3 §5.1, §8.1).

pill.description: The pill, when the line has one.

seq.description: The ledger row it came from: its record.

CallView.description: The exact call a decision is about (spec 3.3 §7.1).

args.description: Its arguments in full, as the inbox shows them to approvers (secrets removed).

text.description: The call as text, `send_email(to: "…", subject: "…")`, cut short when long.

truncated.description: `text` is cut short: the call must be expanded before it can be approved.

CardDetail.description:
A line under a decision's details that a feature adds through a
`CardHint`: where the call comes from, with an optional link into the
home, such as "From the invoice-run workflow · Open in Runs" (spec 3.3 §7.1). Never on a
chat card (S-I5).

href.description:
Where the link goes: a path in the home, such as `/ui/runs/r-1`. A renderer follows only
a path on its own server.

linkText.description: The words of the link after the line: "Open in Runs".

text.description: The line, in plain words: "From the invoice-run workflow".

CardLine.description: One line of an agent's definition on a card: "Area · Home".

mono.description: The value is a technical name, shown in mono. Absent when false.

CardStatus.description: Where a decision is in its life.

leftOut.description:
The upstream components it leaves out, because they could fake a decision or cover
the home.

label.description: What it says: "Version 0.9.1", "No approval controls in drawn UI".

note.description: A line on what it covers.

status.description: How far the home supports it.

ClaimStatus.description: How far a home supports a claim (adk-ui's vocabulary).

oneOf.description: In part; the note says which part.
A release candidate of the protocol, not yet relied on.

ColorChoice.description: A colour a person may choose.

Command.description:
A command from a surface (spec 3.3 §6). Every command runs as an authenticated
`Caller`, whose subject, surface and `Origin` reach its audit record.

§6 also names "steer", a message that reaches a turn while it runs. No runtime under the
engine takes input in the middle of a turn, so there is no steer command: a message sent
during a turn is the session's next message (`Send`), and
`StopAll` stops a turn that has gone wrong.

oneOf.description: Answers a decision at the version the surface saw (S-I2).

expanded.description: The surface showed the call in full (§7.1).

reason.description: Why, for a `deny`; reported to the agent.

oneOf.description: Cancels a spoken "allow once" inside its cancel window (§7.2).
Sends a message; queued instead while a decision of the session is open (S-I4).
Queues a message as the session's next, after its open decisions (S-I4).
Resumes after a stop: the web home or a paired local terminal only (S-I10).
Changes how much a session's agent acts on its own.

Starts a thread with `agent`: the session's first message goes to it, and its
harness stamps the session as its own (spec 3.3 §5.7 "Threads").

agent.description: The agent: a roster row's name.

oneOf.description: Adds an agent by hand, previewed with `digest` (spec 3.3 §5.7).

digest.description: The digest of the preview the person confirmed.

replaces.description: The suggestion **Change it first** replaces, by the agent id it would get.

oneOf.description: Changes an agent at the version seen, previewed with `digest` (spec 3.3 §5.7).

digest.description: The digest of the preview the person confirmed.

oneOf.description: Resumes an agent paused by hand: the web home or a paired local terminal (S-I10).
Removes an agent at the version seen, previewed with `digest` (spec 3.3 §5.7).

digest.description: The digest of the preview that named what ends.

oneOf.description:
Copies one of the person's standing rules to an agent, pinned to it (spec 3.3 §5.7
"Copy one of your rules", S-I19).

Sends a form an agent drew, from the version the person saw (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5):
never runs its tool, but asks for the call, which the drawing agent holds for the
person's decision. Only a person at a screen sends one (`keyboard`, `pointer`,
`touch`). Feature `genui`.

actionId.description: The declared action the person used.

sessionId.description: The session the form is in.

values.description: What the person typed or picked, by the field's data path (`/to`).

oneOf.description: This answer was recorded; `card.decided` says how it ended when it did.
Someone answered first: shown, never retried (S-I2).

decided.description: Who answered, where, how and when.

oneOf.description:
The decision changed since the version the surface saw and is still open: show it
again (S-I2).
A spoken "allow once" takes effect at `cancel_until` unless cancelled (§7.2).
A spoken answer was cancelled in its window.
The message waits until the session's open decisions are answered (S-I4).

position.description: Its place in the queue, from 1.

oneOf.description: The agent was removed; its threads stay.
The agent changed since the version the surface showed: show it again (spec 3.3 §5.7).

text.description: "Finance was changed in the terminal at 10:01".

oneOf.description: A rule was copied to the agent (spec 3.3 S-I19).

A drawn form was sent: its call is on its way to the drawing agent, which holds it for
the person's decision (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5). The form's state follows from that
decision, never from this answer.

CommandRequest.description: `POST /surface/commands` body: the command, the surface it was given on and how.

surface.description: The surface; defaults to the web home.

ComputerPasskey.description: A passkey the person set up on a computer for the web home.

ConfirmOptions.description:
`POST /surface/decisions/{id}/confirm/options` answer: the options for
`navigator.credentials.get`, single use, for two minutes.

challengeId.description: What the confirmation answers, with the assertion.

ConfirmOptionsRequest.description:
`POST /surface/decisions/{id}/confirm/options` body: the answer the person is about to
confirm, bound on the server to this decision, its version and these arguments (spec 3.3
§8.2).

expanded.description: The surface showed the call in full (§7.1).

ConfirmRequest.description: `POST /surface/decisions/{id}/confirm` body: the passkey's assertion for the bound answer.

answer.description: The answer, when the page sends it again: it must be the bound one.

editedArgs.description: The changed arguments, when the page sends them again: they must be the bound ones.

Decided.description:
A decision answered, here or elsewhere (spec 3.3 §8.1 "Decided", §11 S-I2): who answered,
where and how, and when.

by.description: Who answered: "You" for the caller, else the approver's name; empty when nobody did.

scopeText.description:
How far the answer reaches, shown after the text: "done once" for allow once, the
standing rule's label for always allow (spec 3.3 §5.4); `None` when no surface
recorded the answer.

via.description: Where and how, when the answer came through a surface.

oneOf.description: Cancelled or expired without an answer.
Answered, but the source does not say how.

DecisionCard.description:
A decision, drawn the same way on every surface from its inbox entry, never from agent
output (spec 3.3 §7.1, §11 S-I1).

addsAgent.description: The agent a suggestion would add, shown in place of the call (spec 3.3 §5.7, S-I13).

allowed.description: The answers this surface may give; empty once decided.

alsoShown.description: "Also on your phone and in Telegram".

call.description: The exact call: the details under the plain words.

detail.description:
A line under the details from a feature's `CardHint`, such as
"From the invoice-run workflow · Open in Runs" (spec 3.3 §7.1). Never on a chat card
(S-I5).

heading.description: What will happen, in plain words.

id.description: The inbox entry: what a command answers. Never shown.

reversibility.description: Whether it can be taken back.

sessionId.description: The session the call belongs to.

summary.description:
What the heading alone does not say, in plain words, for a decision the kernel itself
asks: who suggests the work and when it runs once allowed, such as "Finance suggests
this. Once you say yes, it runs every 5 minutes." (spec 3.3 §7.1, §8.1). Never on a
chat card (S-I5).

version.description: The version the surface saw, which its answer carries (S-I2). Never shown.

deliveries.description: The latest acknowledged wake-ups, oldest first.

Delivery.description: One wake-up a phone acknowledged, for "Push delivery" (spec 3.3 §5.4).

DrawnActionView.description: A declared action of a drawing, as its button shows it.

args.description: The call's arguments: a field's value, or a constant the drawing fixed.

label.description: The button's label, agent text checked by rule 5.

note.description: The engine's line under the button: "Sending runs send_invoice and asks you first".

DrawnArg.description: One argument of a drawn action's call, as a preview of the call shows it.

path.description: The field whose value it takes, by data path.

value.description: The constant it takes, when it takes no field's value.

DrawnCheck.description:
A check a drawn field makes: the catalog's `required`, `regex`, `length`, `numeric`,
`email`, `and`, `or` and `not` functions, and the message shown when it fails.

condition.description: The A2UI function call that must be true, its bindings at data model paths.

DrawnField.description: A field of a drawing: where its value goes, what it takes and what it checks.

checks.description: What it checks before the form is sent, in order.

max.description: The highest value of a slider, or the latest date.

min.description: The lowest value of a slider, or the earliest date.

path.description:
The data model path its value is at, such as `/to`: the key of its value when the
form is sent.

DrawnInput.description: The kind of value a drawn field takes.

oneOf.description: A date and a time, ISO 8601.

DrawnKind.description:
What a drawing is: a form a person fills in and sends, a card or table to read, or a
screen of catalog components.

oneOf.description: Label and value rows; no buttons.
Any catalog components, with declared actions.

DrawnNode.description:
One component of a drawing, resolved for a renderer: templates expanded, every string a
person reads already in place (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5).

| Component | `text` | `variant` | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | The text | `h1`–`h5`, `caption`, `body` | — |
| `Row`, `Column`, `List` | — | `justify` (Row, Column) or `direction` (List) | `children`; a long `List` has `showAllText` |
| `Card` | — | — | `children` |
| `Tabs` | — | — | `tabs` titles and one child per tab |
| `Divider` | — | `axis` | — |
| `Button` | Its label | `primary`, `default`, `borderless` | `action` |
| `TextField`, `DateTimeInput`, `CheckBox`, `ChoicePicker`, `Slider` | The label | the catalog's variant | `field` |

action.description: The declared action a button asks for.

field.description: A field the person fills in.

key.description:
Unique within the drawing: the component's id, and for a template's copy the list
item it was drawn for, `cell-0@/rows/3`.

showAllText.description: A long list's "Show all 42", when a renderer cuts it.

tabs.description: The titles of a `Tabs`' tabs, one per child.

text.description: What it reads, or its label.

variant.description: A style hint from the catalog.

DrawnOption.description: One option of a drawn choice.

DrawnSent.description:
A person sent a drawn form: the call they asked for, held as the drawing agent for their
decision, or refused by its rules before it was held (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5).

callId.description: The call's id: its result names it.

decisionId.description: The decision it waits on, once held.

held.description: Held for a decision; `false` when the agent's rules refused the call first.

text.description: "Sent at 10:03", or "Finance can't use send_invoice here".

DrawnSurface.description:
A drawing in a thread (spec 3.3 §6.1 `genui`): drawn on the normal card background,
never the decision's, with its strings already resolved on the server.

catalog.description: The catalog it was checked against, such as `forms 1.0`.

changedText.description:
What a newer version says above itself: "Finance changed this form at 10:05", or
"Finance removed this at 10:06" for a removal.

earlierText.description: What this version says once a newer one replaces it: "Earlier version · 10:02".

root.description: What it shows; `None` for a removal.

surfaceId.description: The surface; a later drawing of it is its next version.

title.description: The title, agent text checked by rule 5.

version.description: This version. Only the latest version of a surface is live.

EndedWork.description: What removing an agent ends, counted (spec 3.3 §5.7 "Pausing and removing").

decisions.description: Decisions waiting for you that end without an answer.

text.description:
"Removing Finance stops 1 piece of work, ends 2 decisions waiting for you and 1
routine. Its threads stay."

FeedEntry.description: One event of a session's store, numbered by its position there (spec 3.3 §6).

items.description: What it shows; empty for events with nothing to show.

seq.description:
The event's position in the session store, from 1: the `Last-Event-ID` a surface
resumes from.

FeedFrame.description: One frame of a session's feed (spec 3.3 §6): the snapshot, then the live tail.

oneOf.description: One event of the session store; resume after its `seq` (`Last-Event-ID`).

cards.description: The open decisions of the session.

oneOf.description:
The store's history of the session was replaced (rewound, or deleted and started
again): drop what was shown; the entries follow again from the start.

len.description: How many events the store holds now.

FileUse.description: Where an agent's files are: none, read, or read and change (spec 3.3 §5.7).

FormState.description: A drawn form's state after it was sent (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5).

decisionId.description: The decision it waits on or waited on.

locked.description: Its fields can no longer be changed: it was sent and the call was not refused.

text.description: "Sent at 10:03 · waiting for you", "Sent · done at 10:04", …

FormStatus.description:
Where a drawn form is after it was sent, from its decision and its call's result
(spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5).

oneOf.description: Sent, and the call is held: its decision is not answered here yet.
Sent and answered yes; the call has not finished yet.
Allowed, then refused when it resumed because a rule changed.

The drawing agent's rules refused the call before it was held; the form can be
changed and sent again.
The decision ended without an answer.

forms.description: Each form sent, its latest send per version.

GenuiCapabilities.description:
What `GET /api/surface/genui/capabilities` answers: a table of claims per protocol, and
the catalogs this home renders.

protocols.description: A2UI, AG-UI and MCP Apps, in that order.

GrantedUse.description:
Something the home lets every agent on it do beyond its definition, because the host
gives each agent it runs the tools for it (spec 3.3 §5.7, S-I12, S-I13): shown under
"Here is what Finance can do" as "On this home it can also:". Hosts register each with
`SurfaceEngineBuilder::grant`.

id.description: The feature that grants it, such as `genui`: one line per id. Never shown.

text.description:
What it can do, in plain words: "Ask to change things on your screens — always asks
you first".

InputSource.description: One of the three switches of "What it can see" (spec 3.3 §5.6).

Mode.description: How much agents act on their own (spec 3.3 §8.1).

ModelView.description: A model an agent runs on; never a key (spec 3.3 decision 21).

Origin.description:
How an input was given (spec 3.3 §6, §11): every command carries one, and it reaches the
audit record, so "What your agents did" can say "from Telegram".

oneOf.description: Requested by an agent (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 6: never an answer to a decision).

PasskeyOptions.description:
`POST /surface/phone/passkey/options` answer: the options for
`navigator.credentials.create`, as WebAuthn's JSON form gives them (spec 3.3 §8.2).

publicKey.description:
`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON`: a platform authenticator, user verification
required, attestation none.

registrationId.description: What the registration answers, with the credential.

PhoneDevice.description: A paired device's phone attachments, as "Where you can say yes from" lists them.

passkey.description: It asks for the person's face or fingerprint.

devices.description: Every paired device with a passkey or a push subscription.

PhoneInfo.description:
`GET /surface/phone` answer: what the phone needs to subscribe and to confirm it is you
(spec 3.3 §5.4, §8.2).

canAddPasskey.description:
The caller may set up a passkey now: a phone within 10 minutes of pairing without one,
or the person at the web home.

passkey.description: The caller has a passkey here: this phone's, or for the web home, the person's.

push.description: This phone is subscribed to wake-ups.

pushKey.description: The kernel's push key, which the phone subscribes with (`applicationServerKey`).

rpId.description: The passkeys' relying party: the home's host.

Pill.description: A pill on a briefing line (spec 3.3 §5.1 Today).

claims.description: What this home claims, in order.

PushKeys.description: The keys a browser gives with its push subscription.

p256dh.description: The subscription's P-256 public key, base64url.

PushReceivedRequest.description: `POST /surface/phone/push/received` body: the phone's acknowledgement of a wake-up.

PushSubscriptionRequest.description:
`PUT /surface/phone/push` body: the phone's push subscription, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()`
gives it (spec 3.3 §5.4).

endpoint.description: The push service URL: https, on Apple's, Google's, Mozilla's or Microsoft's service.

QrRequest.description: `POST /surface/phone/qr` body: the pairing link to draw, for the operator.

url.description: The link: it starts with the home's URL.

queued.description:
What the caller typed while a decision of the session was open, oldest first; each is
sent once the session's decisions are answered.

text.description: "Quiet from 22:00", or "Quiet until 07:00" while it holds.

RefusalKind.description: Why a drawing was refused, in a person's terms (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5).

oneOf.description: It shows a decision's words or controls.
It asks for a password or another secret.

It uses something this home does not show: a component outside the catalog, a link,
a function, or a malformed tree.

RefusedDrawing.description:
A drawing that was not shown (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5): a plain notice in the thread; the
technical reason only in the developer panel and the terminal.

agent.description: The agent that tried to draw it.

component.description: The component at fault, when one is.

reason.description:
The technical reason: "catalog forms 1.0 · component c7 Button · label matches
reserved word \"Allow once\" after normalisation".

text.description: "Finance tried to show something that looks like a decision. It wasn't shown."

RemovedAgent.description:
An agent the person removed, whose threads stay readable (spec 3.3 §5.7, §13 decision 18;
owner, at the wave 3 gate: "Removed agents" at the roster's foot).

agent.description: The agent as its threads name it.

RemovedThread.description: One thread of a removed agent, read only.

Reversibility.description: Whether a call can be taken back (spec 3.3 §7.1).

oneOf.description: "Can't be unsent": a message, once sent.
"You can remove it later": an agent a person adds (spec 3.3 §5.7).

"You can change it back": a change a person can make again the other way, such as a
time moved on their screens, which a feature's `CardHint` says
(spec 3.3 §7.1).

Risk.description: How much harm a call can do, as approvers see it (spec 3.3 §7.1).

ShellUse.description: Where an agent's commands run: nowhere, in the sandbox, or on this computer.

Speaker.description: Who wrote a message in a thread.

SpendView.description: Today's spend against the daily limit (spec 3.3 §8.1).

limitMicroUsd.description: The daily spending limit, micro-USD, when set.

text.description: "$1.84 of $5.00 today", or "$1.84 today" with no limit.

StatusLine.description:
The status line every surface shows (spec 3.3 §5.1, §6): the mode word, spend against the
daily limit, quiet time and the count of decisions.

decisions.description: Decisions waiting for the caller: the filled badge.

hostUtcOffsetMinutes.description:
Minutes east of UTC of the server's time zone now: the kernel reads a quiet window that
carries no offset of its own there, so a page in another zone reads it there too
(spec 3.3 §5.1).

mode.description: The mode, when the source runs a harness.

spend.description: Spend, when the source knows it.

StopRequest.description: `POST /surface/stop` body: **Stop all** from a paired device (spec 3.3 §11 S-I10).

SurfaceKind.description:
The surface a person uses (spec 3.3 §5, §7.2).

What a surface may decide is fixed by §7.2 and computed by
`rules::allowed_answers`; a surface never grants more
than the web home.

oneOf.description: The web home installed on a phone (spec 3.3 §5.4).

SurfaceQuery.description: Query of the reads: the surface the answers are computed for.

after.description: `GET .../feed`: resume after this `seq` when no `Last-Event-ID` is sent.

decidedSince.description:
`GET /surface/decisions`: also the decisions answered or ended since then, newest
first, after the open ones (spec 3.3 §5.4).

session.description:
`GET /surface/status`: the session whose mode to show; `GET /surface/decisions`: only
that session's decisions.

surface.description: The surface; defaults to the web home.

TakeOverRequest.description:
`POST /surface/decisions/{id}/take-over` body: the secret typed on a surface, for the card
at the version that surface showed (S-I2). Its `Debug` output redacts the secret.

surface.description: The surface: the web home (default) or the phone, the two that take over (§8.2).

ThreadItem.description:
One thing in a thread (spec 3.3 §5.1): a message, something an agent did, or a decision,
which links to its inbox entry and is drawn from the card (§11 S-I1).

author.description: The author's name: the agent's display name, or "You".

callId.description: The call, to match its result.

oneOf.description: An agent asked first: a held call. Its card comes from the inbox entry.

decisionId.description: The inbox entry, when the call reached the inbox.

oneOf.description:
Something an agent drew (spec 3.3 §6.1 `genui`, §7.4 rule 5): a form, card, table or
screen on the normal card background, never a decision. Only a render tool's result
with the reserved state key and the drawing's digest makes one.

surface.description: The drawing, its strings resolved on the server.

oneOf.description: A drawing that was not shown: a plain notice (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5).

refusal.description: What the thread says, and the reason the developer panel shows.

oneOf.description:
A person sent a drawn form: the call they asked for, held as the drawing agent for
their decision, or refused by its rules (spec 3.3 §7.4 rule 5). The decision's own
`Decision` item follows it in the same entry.

sent.description: The call and the form it came from.

oneOf.description:
An app an MCP server's tool showed (spec 3.3 §6.1 `genui-apps`): on the normal card
background, labelled as unable to approve anything, framed sandboxed by the web home
and shown as its text result elsewhere. Only the event of the MCP tool's own call, which
carries its `adk.mcp.app` record, makes one.

entries.description: Every event of the session store, numbered by position from 1.

TimelineStep.description: One step of how a decision got here (spec 3.3 §7.1).

current.description: The step the decision is at now.

text.description: "Asked at 18:00", "Waited through quiet time", "Waiting for you".

UsesDraft.description: What an agent can use (spec 3.3 §5.7 "What it can use").

drivers.description: The drivers mounted for its area that it may use.

folder.description: One folder inside its area's workspace, relative to it; none for the whole workspace.

Via.description:
Where and how an answer was given, as a decision answered elsewhere shows it
(spec 3.3 §8.1 "Decided").

VoiceClientMessage.description: A text frame the view sends up the voice socket (spec 3.3 §5.6).

oneOf.description: The first message: the ticket `POST /surface/voice/sessions` issued.
A switch of "What it can see" changed; sent before any later frame.
The model's audio finished playing, or was flushed.
End the conversation: a spoken answer in its cancel window is cancelled.
**Cancel** on a spoken screen action in its cancel window (spec 3.3 §5.6).

VoiceModel.description: A realtime model the person can talk on (spec 3.3 §5.6).

inputRate.description: The sample rate of the PCM16 mono audio the model takes.

name.description: The name the select shows, such as "Gemini Live".

outputRate.description: The sample rate of the PCM16 mono audio the model speaks.

VoiceModels.description:
`GET /surface/voice` answer: the models the person can talk on, first the default
(spec 3.3 §5.6).

agent.description: The agent the person talks with, by its display name: "Talking with Chief of staff".

agentName.description:
The agent's name, as `GET /surface/agents` lists it: a conversation opens in Threads
under it when it ends.

VoiceTicket.description:
`POST /surface/voice/sessions` answer (spec 3.3 §5.6).

The ticket works once, within 30 seconds, for the caller it was issued to; the view sends
it in its first message on the socket, never in a URL.

inputRate.description: The sample rate of the audio the view sends up.

outputRate.description: The sample rate of the audio the view plays.

sessionId.description: The voice conversation's session, listed in Threads under the agent.

VoiceTicketRequest.description: `POST /surface/voice/sessions` body: a ticket for the voice socket (spec 3.3 §5.6).

sessionId.description:
Continue this voice conversation instead of starting one: only one of the caller's own
voice sessions (§11 S-I8).

VoiceUpdate.description:
A text frame the server sends down the voice socket: transient voice state only
(spec 3.3 §5.6).

inputRate.description: The sample rate of the audio the view sends up.

outputRate.description: The sample rate of the audio the view plays.

oneOf.description: The model waits for the person.
What the person said, as transcribed.
The decision a spoken answer would apply to now, or none.
A spoken "allow once" takes effect at `cancelUntil` unless cancelled.

A spoken screen action runs at `cancelUntil` unless cancelled (spec 3.3 §5.6): "Snoozing
in 5 s", under the heading "Move News digest to 19:00".

heading.description: What it will do, in the kernel's words: "Move News digest to 19:00".

oneOf.description:
A spoken screen action ended, or was not taken: done, cancelled, refused, or words
that match several things (spec 3.3 §5.6).

actionId.description: The action, when one was pending.

heading.description: What it did or would have done: "Moved News digest to 19:00".

text.description: What happened, in plain words: "Cancelled · nothing changed".

oneOf.description: A spoken answer ended: read the card again for how.

text.description: What happened, in plain words, when it was not recorded.

oneOf.description: The open decisions voice cannot approve: "Decide on screen".
The person spoke over the model: flush the audio not yet played.

code.description: The engine's `surface.*` code, or the source's.

WebUse.description: What of the web an agent reaches.

post.summary: A single-use ticket, good for 30 seconds, for the voice socket `GET /voice/socket` (spec 3.3 §5.6); served with the `voice` feature. The socket's first text message is `{"type":"hello","ticket":…}`; then VoiceClientMessage up and VoiceUpdate down, and binary frames tagged 0x01 (PCM16 audio), 0x02 (camera JPEG) and 0x03 (screen JPEG)
